newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Steel, NKK to up price of China-bound steel.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Steel, NKK to up price of China-bound steel.

text.p: Nippon Steel Corp and NKK Corp said on Thursday that China National Metals & Minerals Import & Export Corp has accepted an increase in the the price of steel products to be shipped to China from August 1997 to January 1998.

Spokesmen for Nippon Steel and NKK said that China has agreed to a five percent rise in the price of cold-rolled sheet, galvanised steel sheet and thick steel sheet from the previous six-month contract, and smaller increases for other steel products.

Nippon Steel has agreed to ship an average of 40,000 tonnes of steel to China per month during the August-January period, up from an average of 25,000 tonnes in the six months to July 1997, the Nippon Steel spokesman said.
"The price increases reflect rising international steel market prices," the Nippon Steel spokesman said.
NKK, while declining to provide the volume of shipments for the six months to January 1998, said the volume would be slightly higher than the preceding six months.
"This (price increase for China-bound steel) will be a positive factor in setting export prices for other areas," the NKK spokesman said.
Kawasaki Steel Corp and Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd have yet to agree with China on steel prices, spokesmen for Kawasaki and Sumitomo said.

Japanese steelmakers are also now seeking an increase in prices for domestic large-lot users such as carmakers and home electronic appliance manufacturers, after lowering prices for large customers over the last five years in response to the yen's appreciation against the dollar.
